observations: Photo 0: Closed black HP laptop with HP logo on lid, placed on top of an HP box. A handwritten note is attached to the lid. Background shows shelves with boxes, some labeled 'MSI'.
Photo 1: Laptop in tent mode, showing keyboard and trackpad. Intel Core sticker visible on lower right of keyboard deck. Background shows more boxes, including MSI and others.

Photo 2: Laptop open in laptop mode, screen on with Windows desktop and colorful default wallpaper. 'Omnibook Ultra' text visible on lower left of keyboard. Intel Core sticker present. Box labeled 'Odyssey OLED' visible beneath laptop. Samsung monitor in background.

claims.evidence: Photo 2 shows 'Omnibook Ultra' text on keyboard, and the device is a 14-inch convertible laptop (shown in tent mode in photo 1).
No visible evidence of Copilot+ PC certification or badge. The Intel Core sticker does not indicate Copilot+ status. This is a software/hardware certification not visible in photos.

Screen is on and appears to be high-resolution and colorful (photo 2), but no visible resolution indicator or OLED badge. Touch capability cannot be confirmed from still photos. The 'OLED' label on the box beneath (photo 2) is for a Samsung Odyssey monitor, not the laptop.
Intel Core sticker is visible in photos 1 and 2, but the specific model 'Ultra 7 256v EVO' is not readable. The sticker does not show the exact model number.

risks.risk: Screen is not OLED or does not have 3K resolution
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the screen bezel or display settings showing resolution and panel type.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a standard FHD or QHD screen, not 3K OLED.

risks.risk: Processor is not Intel Core Ultra 7 256v EVO
risks.proof: Photo of the BIOS screen or system information showing exact CPU model.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a lower-tier Intel Core Ultra 7 or non-EVO model.

risks.proof: Screenshot of Windows Settings > System > About, showing 'Copilot+ PC' designation, or a photo of the Copilot+ badge on the device.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a standard Windows 11 PC, not a Copilot+ device.

risks.proof: Video clip showing finger interaction with the screen (e.g., tapping, swiping).

risks.risk: Device has physical damage or wear not visible in photos
risks.proof: Close-up photos of hinges, screen edges, keyboard, and ports from all angles.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as having potential hidden damage, reducing value.

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the screen bezel or display settings showing resolution and panel type.
Photo of BIOS or system information showing exact CPU model.
Screenshot or photo showing 'Copilot+ PC' designation in Windows Settings.
Close-up photos of hinges, keyboard, ports, and screen edges from all angles.
response.reason: The model is identifiable as HP Omnibook Ultra, but key claims about screen resolution, OLED panel, processor model, and Copilot+ status cannot be verified from current photos. Hidden risks related to screen quality, CPU, and touchscreen functionality affect pricing. Proof is needed to confirm these features before pricing.
